headlines.title: Bay Area weather forecast: Storm to bring rain, hazardous winds and high surf
headlines.description: “Dangerously” high surf is expected along the Bay Area coastline this weekend, with breaking waves ranging from 25 to 35 feet and occasional 50-foot waves at favored break points like Mavericks, according to the National Weather Service. The weather service has issued a high surf warning in anticipation of the massive swells. The warning is slated to go into effect at 6 p.m. Friday and expire at 4 a.m. Sunday. A beach hazards statement already in effect will remain in place until 6 p.m. Friday. The weather service warned of 15- to 20-foot breaking waves, strong rip currents and sneaker waves. The public is asked to stay out of the ocean and away from beaches, jetties, piers, and rocks. “We can’t stress enough how dangerous ocean/beach conditions will be this weekend,” the weather service said in a social media post. “Any wrong move or stumble could turn deadly. No selfie is worth your life. If you need to be rescued, you’re also putting first responders at risk. Know the conditions before you go.” This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.
